floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 10 (build 42 vs 43) reconfirmed; 1-insn gap is a coupled RA load-delay NOP; no sibling analog; frontier = .greg dump + clean-target permuter.

frontier.hypothesis: base->$a3 (instead of $a1) is a resolvable allocno-priority tiebreaker, not a hard liveness conflict.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 local-alloc allocno priority ordering assigns var_v0's test load $a1 first; the .greg conflict list reveals whether base actually conflicts with $a1 or merely lost the priority tie.
frontier.next_probe: cc1 -da on the candidate base.i; read ';; Register dispositions:' for the base and var_v0 pseudos and their conflict sets (the mandated pre-claim diagnostic, never run for this fn).

frontier.hypothesis: A directed/randomized permuter on a clean single-function target closes the a1/a3 swap.
frontier.mechanism: target.o at offset 0 (asm/funcs + prelude, drop .set gp=64) makes the base score the real weighted RA diff instead of ~340k address noise, so the search has usable gradient.
frontier.next_probe: Build clean target.o; run permuter_campaign.py with --stop-on-zero + PERM_* directives; fresh-seed discipline (~20-30 min windows), wait in-turn, harvest --stop before ending.

frontier.hypothesis: Shrinking var_v0's competing live range lets the allocator keep base in $a1.
frontier.mechanism: If var_v0's test-load live range no longer overlaps $a1's assignment window, base (arg-reg-resident, live to the join) wins $a1 and var_v0 falls to $v0.
frontier.next_probe: Derive the specific C form (e.g. delayed materialization / narrowed type of var_v0) from the .greg conflict evidence in frontier item 1, then sandbox + full-build SHA1 check.
